messages.subject: Fwd: specifying a known large covariance matrix in Stan
parts:
Hi all,

Am new to Stan but am trying to fit an animal model using Stan.

I am trying to specify a covariance matrix A for sampling the random effects but Stan reports an error saying its non-symmetric. However using the is.symmetric.matrix() function returns that this matrix is symmetric.

Below is my code for the model:

 stan_code <- '
data {
    int<lower=0> N;
    int<lower=0> b;
    int<lower=0> K;
    int<lower=0> e;
    vector[N] y; // number of observations
    vector[N] beta0; // vector of 1s
    matrix[N,b] X; // fixed eff matrix
    matrix[N,K] Z1; // raneff matrix for BLUPs
    matrix[N,e] Z2; // raneff matrix for envs
    matrix[e,e] Iu;
    matrix[N,N] Ie;
    vector[K] mua;
    vector[e] mue;
}

transformed data {
   cov_matrix[K] A; // Rship matrix
  // A <- cholesky_decompose(A);
}

parameters {
   vector[b] betas;
   vector[K] a;
   vector[e] u;

   real b0; 
   real<lower=0> varb;
   real<lower=0> vara;
   real<lower=0> varu;
   real<lower=0> vare;
   real<lower=0> alpha1;
   real<lower=0> alpha2;
}

//transformed parameters {
  // vector[K] a_real;
  // a_real <- a*alpha1;
   //vector[e] u_real;
   //u_real <- u*alpha2;
//   real vara_r;
//   vara_r <- pow(alpha1,2)* (1/vara)
//   real varu_r;
//   varu_r <- pow(alpha2,2)* (1/varu)
//}
model {
   //for(i in 1:K) mua[i]<- 0;
   //for(i in 1:e) mue[i]<- 0;
   vector[N] mu;
   b0 ~ normal(0,1000);
   alpha1 ~ normal(0,1);
   alpha2 ~ normal(0,1);
   betas ~ normal(b0,varb);
   a ~ multi_normal(mua, (A*vara));
   u ~ multi_normal(mue, (Iu*varu));
   mu <- b0 + X * betas + Z1 * a * alpha1 + Z2 * u * alpha2;
   y ~ multi_normal(mu,(Ie*vare));
}
'
Jmat = rep(1,length(y))
Iu = diag(ncol(Z2))
Ie = diag(length(y))
mua = rep(0,ncol(geno.mat))
mue = rep(0,ncol(Z2))
#options(scipen=100) # make R remove sci notation e+06...
#diag(geno.mat) = diag(geno.mat)+0.02
#hh=chol(geno.mat)
#ss=which(geno.mat < 0.01,arr.ind=T)
#geno.mat[ss]=geno.mat[ss]+0.01

dat <- list(N=length(y) , b=ncol(X), K=ncol(geno.mat), e=ncol(Z2),Iu=Iu, Ie=Ie,
y=y, Z1=Z1, Z2=Z2, X=X, A=geno.mat, beta0=Jmat, mua=mua, mue=mue)


#### do me before running
set_cppo("fast")  # for best running speed

fit <- stan(model_code = stan_code, data = dat, iter = 100, chains = 4)



Thanks.

U.G.O.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Fwd: specifying a known large covariance matrix in Stan
parts:
If by "already a cholesky decomposed matrix," you mean that it's
known and fixed, you can just declare it in the data block as a
cholesky_factor_cov, read it in as data (Stan will verify it's
lower triangular and has positive diagonal entries), and then use
it in multi_normal_cholesky().

If instead, you know the covariance matrix, declare it as cov_matrix,
read it in, then declare a cholesky_factor_cov in transformed data,
and define the cholesky_factor_cov variable as the Cholesky decomposition
of the matrix you read in.

- Bob
